Finding: Persistent public-state writes are not treated as a declassification/observation channel; return/status are checked but CellSet/ArraySet/MapPut are ignored by the policy taint pass and evalContract discards final state.
Impact: Can prove trace/return/status UO while a secret is stored into public state and later observed.
Recommended next step: Extend policy tainting to public writes; add explicit public-state declassification; extend Lean Outcome/history theorem with final public state or public-state delta.

Finding: Loop bounds are documented as compile-time public constants, but lower_for_bound accepts arbitrary right-hand expressions and non-ORAM public loops can escape exact trip-count accounting.
Impact: Secret/state-dependent loop counts can affect gas/time/schedule outside the theorem's fixed public shape.
Recommended next step: Fail closed for all non-constant loop bounds in proof-grade mode, or add sidecar public loop-bound proofs and mechanized admission theorem.

Finding: Sidecar consistency is under-specified: secret_args can silently force an entrypoint confidential even if confidential:false; public entrypoints can still read confidential state subject only to return/status checks.
Impact: Reviewer/operator may believe a sidecar policy is authoritative when compiler normalizes or permits a different confidentiality surface.
Recommended next step: Add MetadataWellFormed: secret_args iff confidential:true; public reads/writes of confidential state only under explicit declassification policy; reject inconsistent sidecars.

Finding: ProofRelevantContractView is large but there is no evident completeness theorem that every runtime-consumed field is included and bound.
Impact: A theorem can validate the serialized view while omitted manifest/artifact fields influence runtime behavior.
Recommended next step: Make proof-relevant view the canonical executable manifest or prove/check field-completeness; add mutation tests for every artifact field.

Finding: Lean accepts runtime proof objects/certificates, but the extraction/completeness of those objects relative to actual executed host I/O remains a trust boundary beyond static drift.
Impact: A self-consistent proof object might omit or misrepresent an executed event beneath the checked boundary.
Recommended next step: Introduce an append-only typed kernel transcript/hash accumulator; derive all proof objects from it and make Lean recompute certificates from the transcript.

Finding: OperationalConfig read/write logic relies on well-formed object ownership; readObject gives public store precedence and unknown objects default public.
Impact: Malformed configs or duplicate/disjointness failures can undermine intended public/secret separation in semantics.
Recommended next step: Add WellFormedConfig with unique object IDs, object-store disjointness, known-object lookups; prove deployment and every step preserve it.

Finding: Nonce/freshness discipline is audited but not proved as a concrete uniqueness property; deterministic deploy_with_seed and diagnostic fresh-coin injection need a hard production/test separation.
Impact: AEAD/ORAM assumptions depend on freshness; accidental seed/nonce reuse would invalidate IND-CPA premises.
Recommended next step: Use domain-separated monotonic nonces or prove CSPRNG stream uniqueness bounds; type-separate production and diagnostic randomness; add CI gate for diagnostic features.

Finding: The claim says real host-visible execution, but the theorem observer is normalized and explicitly excludes raw page IDs, timing, cache, allocator and wall-clock behavior.
Impact: Adopters may overread the SGX side-channel guarantee.
Recommended next step: State the theorem as normalized-host-observer UO, or add raw-to-normalized refinement/modeling for the intended real host observations.

Finding: Abort/rollback and final persistent state are not part of the main outcome theorem even though runtime claims commit/rollback behavior.
Impact: Secret-dependent partial commits or rollback discrepancies could escape the theorem framing.
Recommended next step: Add history/final-state theorem for completed and aborted calls; prove no secret-dependent public persistent effects except declared declassifications.

Finding: Path ORAM local position-map wrapper scans metadata pages in fixed shape; metadata_pages_per_access is metadata_pages+1 with metadata_pages roughly ceil(N/8)+ceil(N/8).
Impact: The theorem-facing Path ORAM backend is effectively linear in map capacity for metadata I/O, limiting large maps.
Recommended next step: Add recursive/private position map or compact private metadata; evaluate scaling to identify practical capacity ceiling.

Finding: Committed validation reports 196 MB materialized canonical pair certificate, 98 MB fresh-coin witness family, and estimates up to 7.08e18 bytes.
Impact: Proof evidence can dominate runtime cost and become infeasible for realistic capacities.
Recommended next step: Replace enumerated certificate families with symbolic/parameterized certificates, streaming checks, or compact seed-based proofs.

Finding: encrypted_to_client returns are rejected; confidential calls can only return public/declassified values or no secret payload.
Impact: Many useful confidential applications need private result delivery to a client.
Recommended next step: Implement attested encrypted return channel with nonce/session-key evidence and a Lean policy theorem for encrypted outputs.

Finding: Current committed runtime overhead result contains only one overhead case, although correctness/leakage files cover more toy benchmarks.
Impact: Adoption decision cannot infer scaling, latency, or capacity cost from the existing result bundle.
Recommended next step: Run a capacity/backends/workload matrix with latency, bytes, proof cost, artifact size, and leakage metrics.
